newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn sympathetic to Syria, foreign minister says.
newsitem.headline: Bonn sympathetic to Syria, foreign minister says.

text.p: Germany has great sympathy for Syria's position towards Israel and is also interested in playing a more political role in the Middle East peace process, Syrian Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara said on Wednesday.

Al-Shara said a tour of European cities had also convinced him the European Union was concerned about Israel's policies, even if it was not saying so publicly, and that there was considerable sympathy for Damascus.
"I can say that the European stance has improved regarding the Middle East and the search for a just peace," Al-Shara told a news conference in Bonn.

Peace talks between Israel and Syria broke off a year ago. Damascus insists the talks cannot resume unless Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu accepts the outcome of previous negotiations with the old Labour-led government.

Syria says the former Israeli government, which was defeated by Netanyahu in elections last May, had agreed during talks with Damascus to withdraw fully from the Golan Heights, captured by Israel in 1967.

Al-Shara held talks in Germany with Chancellor Helmut Kohl, President Roman Herzog and Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel during a three-day visit. He said Kohl was "pessimistic" about the state of the peace process.
"Whether Germany says it openly or not, I have drawn the conclusion they are concerned about the peace process and the policies that have led to this situation," Al-Shara said.
"I also sensed Germany is interested in playing a political role in the Middle East, as well as an economic one. That would be a positive development, in my opinion," the minister said.
Al-Shara came to Germany after accompanying Vice-President Abdel-Halim Khaddam on a European tour which officials said included the Netherlands, Ireland and France.
